title: Streamlined adaptive batcher with KV pressure feedback for mixed-length workloads
creator: Oliver Park
description: Tuning the continuous batching scheduler to more gracefully handle heavily mixed prompt/response length distributions while preventing KV cache thrashing and reducing GPU memory fragmentation. The goal is consistent P50/P95 latency within SLOs, higher average throughput, and reduced GPU memory headroom waste across heterogeneous inference workloads.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token-generation latency not increased by more than 5% for 95% of production routes after rollout
KV cache hit rate improvement or stable (no more than 2% drop) across mixed-length routes
Average GPU memory overhead (headroom reserved) reduced by >=10% on observed clusters
No increase in tail OOM incidents post-canary; safe rollback plan validated
Automated metrics and dashboards created: kv_eviction_rate, kv_hit_rate, batch_coalesce_rate, p50/p95 latency per route
notes: Background: current continuous batcher uses fixed slot allocation with greedy coalescing that performs poorly on distributions with a long tail of long responses (chat sessions) mixed with many short prompts (search/qa).
Primary risks: heavy eviction churn on KV cache leading to increased token compute; GPU memory fragmentation causing lower packing efficiency and occasional OOMs under bursty traffic.
progress_updates: 2026-03-11 - Spike completed: simulated mixed-length traces (80% < 32 tokens, 15% 128-512 tokens, 5% >1024 tokens) and measured eviction hysteresis impact. Observed 18% throughput regression with current greedy coalescer due to KV churn.
2026-03-11 - Implemented prototype feedback loop: batcher reads per-GPU KV eviction watermark and reduces coalescing aggressiveness when eviction_rate > 150 evictions/min.

2026-03-12 - Local cluster test (4x A100): prototype reduced eviction rate by 42% and improved effective KV hit rate by 9% for synthetic skewed-dialog workload. P95 improved by 40ms on average but coarse-grained slot resizing caused some 99th percentile spikes.

2026-03-12 - Added instrumentation hooks: kv_pressure (low|medium|high), dynamic_slot_resize_count, batch_merge_attempts, kv_eviction_rate_per_min. Dashboards PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-dashboard/pull/88
2026-03-12 - Canaries scheduled on dev region next: route 'chat-long-tail' and 'qa-short-prompt' with 10% traffic for 48 hours. Launch runbook created.
experiments: length-histogram-matching: maintain per-route histograms and prefer merging requests whose predicted token lengths fall within the same length bucket (8/32/128/512/2048). Result: more stable batch shapes, small latency increase for some short requests but lower KV churn.

kv-watermark-feedback: if kv_eviction_rate > threshold, reduce max_coalesce_window_ms from 10ms -> 3ms and reduce slot_merge_priority for large-slot candidates. Result: eviction rate down, more small batches sent, minimal P50 impact.

slot-compaction: periodically compact free KV slab segments when GPU idle time > 50ms to reduce fragmentation. Trade-off: compaction pauses (stop-the-world microseconds) vs smoother long-term packing.

weighted-scheduling: prefer shorter prompt requests into fast-path lanes with reserved KV budget; long responses routed to slower but larger-slot lanes. Observed 12% overall cost reduction in sim for mixed workloads.

soft-prefetch: prefetch KV prefixes for sessions with high continuity probability (session affinity) to increase hit-rate on long chats. Increased prefetch network IO by 6% but improved hit-rate by 7%.
decisions: Adopt hybrid policy: length-histogram matching + KV pressure feedback as primary controls. Rationale: gives predictable batching shapes while reacting to runtime memory pressure.
Default coalesce window reduced to 6ms across the fleet, but per-route overrides allowed through route config to avoid regressions on latency-sensitive short-prompt services.
Introduce three KV watermarks (low/medium/high) mapped to different coalescing aggressiveness levels; thresholds to be tuned per-hardware class.
Enable slot compaction opportunistically during quiet windows; compaction limited to <2% of GPU utilization to avoid interference.
Expose route-level knobs in console: coalesce_window_ms, length_bucketing_enabled, kv_pressure_cascade (low/med/high).
metrics_baseline: Baseline (prod sample window 2026-02-15..2026-02-22): p50 token latency 18ms, p95 token latency 78ms, kv_hit_rate 71%, kv_eviction_rate 220/min per GPU in worst clusters, average GPU headroom reserved 14%.
canary_plan: Deploy to dev region A with 10% traffic split for two target routes. Monitor kv_eviction_rate, kv_hit_rate, p50/p95 latency, gpu_memory_free_percent. Criteria to expand to staging: no increase >5% in p95, no new OOMs, kv_eviction_rate <= baseline. Rollback if either OOM or p95 increase >10% sustained for 5 minutes.
rollback_plan: Revert scheduler flags at control-plane config (fast rollback route-level): set coalesce_window_ms back to fleet default, disable length_bucketing and revert slot compaction schedule. Automated scripts to restore previous policy in under 2 minutes.
